title: Ace settings
description: Settings for how Ace behaves in this project, in ace/config.json. A missing file or a missing key uses the default. The files in ace/ say how this project does a job. These settings say how much agents do on their own, and which optional Ace features are on.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, so your editor checks the file and explains each key.

autonomy.description: How much agents do without a person: who sets a ticket ready, which findings ace-review and ace-babysit-pr fix, and what happens to a ticket ace-work-ticket rejects as already done or wrong.
enumDescriptions: A person sets every ticket ready, reviews fix nothing, and a rejected ticket waits for a person.

A person sets every ticket ready, automated or fix-requested reviews fix what has one clearly correct fix (interactive reviews stay read-only and offer fixes locally), and a rejected ticket waits for a person.

Tickets from a plan a person approved go ready on their own, automated or fix-requested reviews also pick a fix when several are reasonable, and ace-work-ticket closes a ticket it rejects. Tickets from ace-audit still wait for a person.

communication.description: How Ace talks to the user in chat replies and pull request explainers. Posted pull request review comments, commits, audit tickets, and ace/ files keep code references for agents.
enumDescriptions: Refer to files, lines, symbols, and code as needed.
Speak in user-facing behavior, flows, and glossary terms. Omit file paths, line numbers, function or symbol names, code snippets, and raw stack traces, unless the user asks for them.

ticket_tracker.description: A built-in ticket tracker. Without this key, Ace uses ace/TICKET_TRACKER.md when it exists, such as for Linear or Jira, and otherwise writes each ticket into the reply. With it, ace/TICKET_TRACKER.md replaces only the sections it holds.
enumDescriptions: GitHub Issues, through the gh CLI. Ace ships how to read, open, and update tickets.

review.description: How ace-review runs. A review is best run by a model other than the one that built the change.

require_other_model.description: When true, a session never reviews a change it built: it gives the line to send to another model, such as a new session on a different model or the user's runner. When false, it reviews the change on request and adds a one-line tip that a different model catches more.

pull_requests.description: How big a pull request may get, so a person and ace-review can still review it.

max_added_lines.description: The most lines one pull request may add. Binary files, lockfiles, snapshots, and files .gitattributes marks linguist-generated do not count. ace-to-ticket sizes tickets to fit, ace-implement stops to propose a cut when it nears the limit, and ace-open-pr pushes nothing past it unless the user says so. 0 turns the limit off.

write_adrs.description: Record architecture decisions in ace/adrs/. When true, ace-grill writes an ADR for each settled decision that is hard to reverse, surprising without its context, and the result of a real trade-off. ace-explain and ace-implement read ADRs whenever ace/adrs/ exists, whatever this says.
